entries.capsule: Minnesota's day, set in state law, to honor Hmong who served in the Secret War in Laos, 1961 to 1975.
entries.dateRule: May 14 each year, by Minnesota statute. If it falls on a weekend, schools are encouraged to mark it the Friday before.
entries.whatItMarks: May 14, 1975, when the American-trained Hmong command structure ceased operating. It honors those who served in the Secret War. General Vang Pao's departure from Laos, as named in the seed entry, is the same event in many accounts, but the statute frames the day around the Special Guerrilla Units.
entries.howCelebrated: By law the governor issues a proclamation and orders flags at half-staff on Capitol grounds; schools are encouraged to teach Hmong history. St. Paul Public Schools suggests books, traditional clothing, displays and music for Hmong American Day. Its 2019 sponsor, Rep. Tou Xiong, hoped schools would use the day to teach the war. A 2026 bill for a Hmong Heritage Week, May 14 to 20, was at the introduction stage when checked.
entries.workplaceNote: Minn. Stat. 10.5805 says businesses may close in honor of this day and an employee may request the day off in observance. It does not make the day a paid or required holiday in the wording checked.

Greater Minnesota holds its own: Albert Lea at Southwest Middle School (January 2018) and Albert Lea High School (December 2025, several hundred people, with the mayor and superintendent), and Worthington's Karen Community at St. Mary's School on Jan. 1, 2024. entries.howCelebrated: Reports show a pattern rather than one Somali-only event. Eid prayers draw large crowds at shared Muslim sites: CBS Minnesota reported tens of thousands at the Minneapolis Convention Center on June 28, 2023, quoting the executive director of Abubakar As-Saddique Islamic Center, and 'Super Eid' filled U.S. Bank Stadium in 2018 and on July 9, 2022. Sahan Journal reported in 2020 that some Muslims, including a Somali Minnesotan, perform the sacrifice at farms such as Meat Halal Farm in Braham, and in 2021 that Minneapolis bakeries make thousands of pounds of halwa for the holiday. entries.name: Christmas on the Julian calendar (January 7)
entries.capsule: Christmas as kept on January 7 by churches and families that still follow the older Julian church calendar.
entries.dateRule: December 25 on the Julian calendar, which is January 7 on the civil calendar from 1900 to 2099. Since 2023 the Orthodox Church of Ukraine, the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church and Ukraine's government have moved to December 25, so many Ukrainian families now keep Dec. 25; others keep Jan. 7. Ask the family.
entries.whatItMarks: The birth of Jesus, with Holy Supper (Sviat Vechir) on Christmas Eve.
entries.howCelebrated: No opened Minnesota source describes a Jan. 7 celebration in 2026. St. Constantine Ukrainian Catholic Church in Minneapolis adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1943 and keeps Dec. 25. Which date each Minnesota Ukrainian Orthodox parish now uses could not be confirmed.

entries.whatItMarks: The birth of Jesus.
entries.howCelebrated: St. Constantine Ukrainian Catholic Church adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1943, so its Christmas falls on Dec. 25. No opened 2026 Minnesota Christmas event listing was found.
